claim: One frozen topic-query title/abstract BM25 baseline versus predeclared seeded random permutations on 3 text-bearing retrospective research topics; effect size and null results are retained.
priorArt: Okapi BM25 information retrieval; no novel mathematical theorem
ASReview active learning not implemented or measured
sourceRights: The fork's index.csv reports 'custom open license' for each Cohen task. Only authorized metadata analysis and aggregate summaries; do not republish original abstracts or license commercially without independent original terms review.

selection.reason: Three bounded small text-bearing corpora from the same source collection; intentionally diverse drug-review topics, not independent disciplines, no cherry-picked tasks after model performance.

labels.unknown: refuse nonbinary label; missing text remains visible and in denominators

metric.endpoint: retrospective ranking workload to encounter ceil(.95*total positives) with oracle-revealed labels
metric.recallAt20Pct: positive labels in top ceil(.2*N) / total positive labels
metric.randomAlgorithm: Fisher-Yates with Xorshift32 seeded by 20261027 plus ordinal, deterministic; derive distribution and compare not a trained ASReview engine
metric.query: Frozen topical query, not tuned using inclusion labels
metric.lexicalMethod: BM25 k1=1.2,b=0.75 on title twice plus abstract once; ASCII lowercase words; ties by original PMID ascending; IDF from unlabeled corpus only
metric.missingTitleAbstract: source rows remain even if no text; score zero

limits: All three tasks are drawn from one original Cohen review collection; cross-disciplinary generalization is not established.
Query terms are source-topic-informed but not learned from hidden labels.
The retrospective oracle metric knows total positives; it is not a production stopping rule.
No reviewer or vendor ASReview model actually benchmarked.
Source rights, including abstracts, are not inferred from the source fork's MIT code license.
This initial result has no prespecified superiority margin or claim of commercial parity.
